architecture.AR-01: Root CA is offline, standalone, non-domain-joined, self-signed: the trust anchor
architecture.AR-02: Root CA signs only issuing CA certificates (offline ceremony) and its own CRL
architecture.AR-03: Issuing CAs are enterprise subordinate CAs, signed by the root, CA=true, not trust anchors
architecture.AR-04: RDPAuth is published only on Issuing CA 1; WebServer-TLS only on Issuing CA 2
architecture.AR-05: AD authenticates requesters, stores templates/permissions/Enrollment Services, distributes the root
architecture.AR-06: AIA and CDP are HTTP locations on the PKI HTTP host, embedded in issued certificates
architecture.AR-07: OCSP appears only as 'if an Online Responder is deployed'

facts.F-01: The user initiates RDP; the RDP server owns and presents the RDP certificate
facts.F-02: Out of the box RDP uses a self-signed certificate the client cannot verify
facts.F-03: Key pairs are generated locally; private keys (including CA keys) never leave their owner
facts.F-04: The request contains the public key, is signed with the private key, never contains it
facts.F-05: RDP enrollment is policy-triggered; eligible CAs are discovered from AD before sending
facts.F-06: The CA authenticates, checks publication, Enroll permission and template policy before signing
facts.F-07: RDPAuth builds subject/SAN from AD; WebServer-TLS takes the subject from the request
facts.F-08: RDPAuth uses Remote Desktop Authentication EKU; WebServer-TLS uses Server Authentication
facts.F-09: The issued certificate goes to LocalMachine\My beside the existing private key
facts.F-10: In TLS the server sends its chain and proves possession of the private key by signing
facts.F-11: The client builds the chain to a root already trusted; AIA may fetch, never creates trust
facts.F-12: Validation is a set of distinct checks; the name match is a separate identity check
facts.F-13: Revocation is checked for each non-root link via CDP/CRL; the root is not checked
facts.F-14: Different templates can be issued by different eligible issuing CAs
facts.F-15: Both issuing paths terminate at the same Root CA
facts.F-16: Kerberos server authentication is out of scope on screen; the film shows certificate-based auth
facts.F-17: Terminology: end-entity certificate, subordinate/intermediate issuing CA, trust anchor = root

cinematic.C-02: One continuous camera; no hard cuts except the S5 flashback
cinematic.C-03: One clear focal subject per shot
cinematic.C-04: Foreground, midground and background layers with parallax
cinematic.C-06: Eased motion; no pops or jitter; exits slightly faster than entrances
cinematic.C-08: Restraint in glow, haze and particles

legibility.L-01: Caption cap height >= 30 px; must-read in-world labels >= 18 px at 1080p
legibility.L-02: Contrast >= 4.5:1 against the sampled local background
legibility.L-03: All text inside the 90% title-safe area
legibility.L-04: Each caption on screen >= max(2.5 s, 0.35 s per word)
legibility.L-05: One caption at a time, never covering the focal action
legibility.L-06: In-world names readable at the moment they matter
legibility.L-07: Role colours distinguishable (CIEDE2000 >= 15), including under CVD simulation

scenes.title: An identity the client can't verify
Finding the right CA, then evaluation
The hierarchy and the trust anchor

beats.title: User opens RDP
beats.summary: At CLIENT01 the user opens an RDP connection to rdp01.1sn0s.lab.

beats.title: Connection pulse
beats.summary: An amber connection pulse travels the floor light-channel to the RDP server.

beats.title: Listener lights
beats.summary: Arrival at rdp01.1sn0s.lab; the RDP listener lights up.

beats.title: Self-signed, unverified
beats.summary: The server's out-of-the-box self-signed certificate reaches the client, which cannot verify it; nothing is accepted and the attempt closes.

beats.title: Template from policy
beats.summary: Group Policy names the RDPAuth template for the RDP server.

beats.title: Key pair forms
beats.summary: A new key pair is generated inside the RDP server chassis.

beats.title: Private key anchored
beats.summary: The private key settles into the server's locked key container and stays there.

beats.title: Request assembled
beats.summary: The public key and request information enter the request capsule.

beats.title: Proof of possession
beats.summary: The private key signs the request in place; the key does not move.

beats.title: Who publishes the template?
beats.summary: The enrollment client asks AD (1SN0S.LAB) which CA publishes RDPAuth; only Issuing CA 1 is eligible.

beats.title: Into Issuing CA 1
beats.summary: The request travels to Issuing CA 1 only.

beats.title: Four checks
beats.summary: Issuing CA 1 authenticates the requester and checks publication, Enroll permission and template policy.

beats.title: CA signs
beats.summary: The request is consumed; Issuing CA 1's key, sealed in its module, drives the press that signs the end-entity certificate.

beats.title: Certificate installed
beats.summary: The certificate returns and locks in beside the existing private key.

beats.title: The trust anchor
beats.summary: A sealed, cable-free gold vault: 1SN0S Root CA, self-signed, offline.

beats.title: Offline ceremony (flashback)
beats.summary: Earlier, at setup: Issuing CA 1's own CA request is carried to the root on removable media; the root issues and signs Issuing CA 1's CA certificate offline, and the certificate is carried back.

beats.title: Issuer link
beats.summary: Present: a gold-to-cyan link joins Issuing CA 1's certificate to the root. No end-entity request reaches the root.

beats.title: Presentation
beats.summary: A new connection attempt: the server presents its certificate with Issuing CA 1's certificate and proves possession of its private key.

beats.title: Chain builds
beats.summary: On the client the cards dock upward to a root already in the Trusted Root store, installed earlier by policy.

beats.title: AIA is not trust
beats.summary: A small AIA indicator: a missing intermediate could be fetched; fetching never creates trust.

beats.title: Validation checks
beats.summary: Chain, signatures, validity, name, EKU resolve; revocation is pending.

beats.title: Revocation per link
beats.summary: Two CRL fetches from the CDP, one per non-root link; OCSP only if deployed.

beats.title: Trusted session
beats.summary: The channel turns green and the RDP session opens.

beats.title: Web server
beats.summary: WEB01 serves portal.1sn0s.lab and needs a WebServer-TLS certificate.

beats.title: Local key, sealed request
beats.summary: A local key pair; the private key is anchored; the request is sealed by proof of possession.

beats.title: Eligibility
beats.summary: AD shows both CAs: Issuing CA 1 does not publish WebServer-TLS; Issuing CA 2 is eligible.

beats.title: Only to Issuing CA 2
beats.summary: The request travels only to Issuing CA 2.

beats.title: Compressed checks
beats.summary: Issuing CA 2 runs the four checks; the subject is supplied in the request, so enrollment is restricted.

beats.title: TLS certificate
beats.summary: Issuing CA 2's key-driven press signs the TLS certificate; it locks in beside the web server's private key.

beats.title: Same root
beats.summary: Issuing CA 2's own certificate is linked in gold to the same root.

beats.title: Browser validation
beats.summary: A browser validates portal.1sn0s.lab up to the root; the channel turns green.

beats.title: Hero topology
beats.summary: Root on top, both issuing CAs, both servers and the user; cyan and violet paths converge in gold at one root.

beats.title: Close
beats.summary: Closing captions and title card; gentle settle and fade.
